Australia’s Ben Treloar is one of the two on-field umpires in the ongoing Ranji Trophy fixture between Delhi and Gujarat at the Palam ‘B’ ground . The 44-year-old is in Delhi as part of an exchange programme between Cricket Australia (CA) and the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI).
Treloar has considerable experience in his locker, having officiated in 30 First Class, 20 List-A and 39 Big Bash League games. He has also stood in two Women’s One-Day Internationals (ODIs) and four Women’s T20Is.
Away from the field, Treloar works as Cricket New South Wales’ Umpire Education Officer, where he grooms the next generation of umpires. Treloar will officiate two Ranji games, with his next assignment being Mumbai against Haryana in Mumbai from October 26 to 29.
The exchange will see Indian umpire Parashar Joshi travel to Australia to stand in two Sheffield Shield matches and a One-Day Cup fixture.
Joshi, who hails from Maharashtra, has been part of the Indian domestic system for some time. His credentials include 19 First Class appearances in the Ranji Trophy and Duleep Trophy, 32 List-A matches and 40 T20s. He has also umpired games in the Indian Premier League (IPL).
